1.blurb: Meanwhile in Ancient Korea: this is the world Goryeo climbed out of. Unified Silla froze under the rigid bone-rank caste order; by the late 800s that closed aristocracy was killing its own kings while the countryside broke apart into the Later Three Kingdoms — the wreck Wang Geon rebuilt into Goryeo.

1.matchText: the warring patchwork historians call the Five Dynasties
1.blurb: Meanwhile in Tang–Song China: the brilliant Tang dynasty had disintegrated in 907 into the warring patchwork of the Five Dynasties. It is from that mid-collapse China, and soon the reunifying Song, that Goryeo borrows its examinations, ministries, and statecraft over the next two chapters.

1.matchText: Viking fleets were raiding and settling
1.blurb: Meanwhile in the Viking Age: as Wang Geon bound his warlords by marriage on the far side of Asia, Norse fleets were raiding and settling from the English coast to the river-roads of what would become Russia. Goryeo was founded into the same generation that watched the last Carolingians fade and the Kievan Rus' take shape.

Meanwhile in the Byzantine Empire: while Europe fragmented, the one large, orderly Christian power sat near its Macedonian height in Constantinople, a bureaucratic, literate, ceremonial state that, like the Goryeo being founded in the same decades, ran on a trained official class rather than purely on warlords.

2.blurb: Meanwhile in Joseon Korea: the civil service examination Gwangjong installed in 958 outlived Goryeo entirely. The Joseon dynasty inherited the gwageo and made it the unchallenged spine of the state, running exam halls and a Confucian officialdom for five more centuries.

Meanwhile in Dai Viet: Vietnam joined the same small club, founding a Confucian examination system in 1075 under the Ly dynasty. Korea and Vietnam are the two states outside China that built lasting exam-selected bureaucracies on the Chinese model, an inheritance Western Europe would not match for nearly a thousand years.

2.matchText: the world's first government paper money
2.blurb: Meanwhile in Tang–Song China: Song China was running a roaring cash economy and in 1024 issued the world's first government paper money, possible only because dense commerce already needed it. Goryeo could copy Chinese ministries and exams by decree but could not decree the market beneath them into existence, and its iron coins simply failed.

3.blurb: Meanwhile in Ancient Korea: Gang Gam-chan's trap at Gwiju, draw the bigger invader deep, starve it, then annihilate the exhausted remnant on its way out, was almost exactly the maneuver Goguryeo's Eulji Mundeok used to destroy a vast Sui Chinese army at the Salsu River in 612. A recurring Korean answer to being outnumbered.

4.matchText: crushed the very Liao empire that had once terrified Goryeo
4.blurb: The Liao ruling family did not simply vanish when the Jurchen Jin destroyed them. A Khitan prince, Yelü Dashi, fled west with a remnant force and founded the Qara-Khitai — a new Central Asian empire that ruled Samarkand and Bukhara for a century. That unlikely westward escape and the Buddhist empire it built, tolerant of its Muslim subjects, is the subject of the Uyghur Steppe chapter on the Qara-Khitai.

5.blurb: Meanwhile in the Mongol Empire: the power Goryeo first met in 1219 as a useful ally against Khitan remnants was the empire Genghis Khan himself was then exploding out of the steppe, breaking states from China to Persia to the Rus'. The bill it presented to Goryeo, tribute and overbearing envoys, was the prelude to the catastrophe of the next chapter.

6.blurb: Meanwhile in the Mongol Empire: by the 1230s the Mongols had built the largest contiguous land empire in history, having already shattered the Jin, the Khwarazmians, and the Rus' principalities. Goryeo faced this with a sixty-year military dictatorship and a border wall built to stop Khitan cavalry, and survived only by retreating to a tidal island.

Meanwhile in the Mongol Empire: the Goryeo crown prince bet on Kublai during the Mongol succession war, and Kublai won, founding the Yuan dynasty that would rule China. Because of that personal gamble Goryeo alone among the major settled states the Mongols fought kept its own royal house, a privileged vassal rather than an erased province.

7.matchText: leave conquered dynasties on their thrones
7.blurb: Meanwhile in the Mongol Empire: the Mongols normally annexed and erased the states they conquered — the Jin under Ögedei, and finally the Song under Kublai. Goryeo alone kept its own royal house, as a Yuan 'son-in-law nation' married into Kublai's family, the unique exception bought by one Goryeo prince's early bet on Kublai during his succession war.

7.matchText: the required orthodoxy of the Chinese civil examinations
7.blurb: Meanwhile in Tang–Song China: Zhu Xi built Neo-Confucianism in Song China as a total theory of reality. In 1313 the Mongol Yuan made his commentaries the required orthodoxy of the Chinese examinations, so the ideology reached Goryeo welded to a credential and a career, the intellectual bomb that would, a century on, blow up the dynasty.

8.blurb: Meanwhile in the Ming dynasty: the Red Turban rebels who spilled into Korea and sacked Gaegyeong in 1361 belonged to the same millenarian anti-Yuan rising that, in China, eventually produced the Ming dynasty. The new Ming would then demand Goryeo's recovered northeast, the order that sent Yi Seong-gye marching toward the Yalu.

8.matchText: the chief architect of the dynasty that follows
8.blurb: Meanwhile in Joseon Korea: Jeong Do-jeon, the radical Neo-Confucian theorist who argued a dynasty losing the people's trust forfeits the right to rule, became the chief architect of the Joseon state. Goryeo's afterlife was its replacement; the next TL opens with the Wihwado Retreat and the dynasty Yi Seong-gye founded.
